---- MODULE W4Od5m8p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Players, Tables
VARIABLES lobbyLock, tableLock, admin, seated

NoOne == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ lobbyLock \in Players \cup {NoOne}
    /\ tableLock \in [Tables -> Players \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN
    /\ seated \in SUBSET Players

GrabLobby ==
    /\ lobbyLock = NoOne
    /\ \E p \in Players : lobbyLock' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tableLock, admin, seated>>

GrabTable ==
    /\ lobbyLock # NoOne
    /\ \E t \in Tables :
         /\ tableLock[t] = NoOne
         /\ tableLock' = [tableLock EXCEPT ![t] = lobbyLock]
         /\ seated' = seated \cup {lobbyLock}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, admin>>

ReleaseTable ==
    /\ \E t \in Tables :
         /\ tableLock[t] = lobbyLock
         /\ lobbyLock # NoOne
         /\ tableLock' = [tableLock EXCEPT ![t] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, admin, seated>>

ReleaseLobby ==
    /\ lobbyLock # NoOne
    /\ \A t \in Tables : tableLock[t] # lobbyLock
    /\ lobbyLock' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tableLock, admin, seated>>

AdminOn ==
    /\ ~admin
    /\ admin' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, tableLock, seated>>

AdminSeat ==
    /\ admin
    /\ \E t \in Tables, p \in Players :
         /\ tableLock[t] = NoOne
         /\ tableLock' = [tableLock EXCEPT ![t] = p]
         /\ seated' = seated \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, admin>>

AdminOff ==
    /\ admin
    /\ \A t \in Tables : tableLock[t] = NoOne \/ tableLock[t] = lobbyLock
    /\ admin' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, tableLock, seated>>

Next == GrabLobby \/ GrabTable \/ ReleaseTable \/ ReleaseLobby
        \/ AdminOn \/ AdminSeat \/ AdminOff

vars == <<lobbyLock, tableLock, admin, seated>>
Init ==
    /\ lobbyLock = NoOne
    /\ tableLock = [t \in Tables |-> NoOne]
    /\ admin = FALSE
    /\ seated = {}

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A fine (table) lock may only be held by the player currently holding the
\* coarse lobby lock, unless the admin override is engaged.
OnlyAuthorizedHoldsTable ==
    \A t \in Tables :
        tableLock[t] # NoOne =>
            (tableLock[t] = lobbyLock \/ admin)
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker uses a two-level hierarchical lock so that players claim resources coarse-to-fine. To touch any individual table a player must first hold the single lobby lock (the coarse lock); only then may that same player claim a free table's fine lock. A player releases its tables before releasing the lobby lock, so the coarse lock always dominates the fine ones. A privileged admin override exists: when engaged, an administrator may seat any player at any free table directly, bypassing the lobby lock, and the override can only be disengaged once every table it touched has been cleared or belongs to the current lobby holder. The concern is that a table must never end up locked by a participant who has no authority to hold it -- that is, someone who does not currently hold the lobby lock while the admin override is off.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state, any table whose fine lock is held is held by the player currently holding the lobby lock, unless the admin override is engaged.

---- MODULE W4Od16m5p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Nodes, Scripts, Bins, Quorum
VARIABLES votes, binOwner, scriptBin, crashed

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ votes \in [Scripts -> SUBSET Nodes]
    /\ binOwner \in [Bins -> Scripts \cup {None}]
    /\ scriptBin \in [Scripts -> Bins \cup {None}]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Nodes

CastVote ==
    /\ \E n \in Nodes, s \in Scripts :
         /\ n \notin crashed
         /\ n \notin votes[s]
         /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = votes[s] \cup {n}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<binOwner, scriptBin, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
    /\ \E n \in Nodes : crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, binOwner, scriptBin>>

Dispense ==
    /\ \E s \in Scripts, b \in Bins :
         /\ Cardinality(votes[s]) >= Quorum
         /\ scriptBin[s] = None
         /\ binOwner[b] = None
         /\ binOwner' = [binOwner EXCEPT ![b] = s]
         /\ scriptBin' = [scriptBin EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

Complete ==
    /\ \E s \in Scripts :
         /\ scriptBin[s] # None
         /\ binOwner' = [binOwner EXCEPT ![scriptBin[s]] = None]
         /\ scriptBin' = [scriptBin EXCEPT ![s] = None]
         /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed>>

Next == CastVote \/ Crash \/ Dispense \/ Complete

vars == <<votes, binOwner, scriptBin, crashed>>
Init ==
    /\ votes = [s \in Scripts |-> {}]
    /\ binOwner = [b \in Bins |-> None]
    /\ scriptBin = [s \in Scripts |-> None]
    /\ crashed = {}

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The bin-to-script and script-to-bin maps stay mutual inverses, so a bin is
\* never held by two scripts and a script never occupies two bins at once.
AllocationConsistent ==
    /\ \A b \in Bins : binOwner[b] # None => scriptBin[binOwner[b]] = b
    /\ \A s \in Scripts : scriptBin[s] # None => binOwner[scriptBin[s]] = s
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser is controlled by a small cluster of pharmacist nodes that must reach a quorum before any medication bin is committed to a prescription. Each node may cast a vote for a given prescription script, and only once a quorum of votes has accumulated may the system allocate a free bin to that script. When a script is later completed, its bin is freed and its votes are reset so the bin can serve another prescription. One node may crash silently at any time and simply stops casting votes; the remaining nodes must still be able to form a quorum. The critical concern is that a single bin must never be committed to two different prescriptions, and a prescription must never simultaneously occupy two bins -- the bin assignment must stay a clean one-to-one mapping.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the bin-owner and script-bin assignments are mutual inverses, so no bin is double-allocated to two scripts.

---- MODULE W4Od3m7p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Banks, MaxVer
VARIABLES regVal, regVer, reqs, writerLog

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ regVal \in Nat
    /\ regVer \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ reqs \in SUBSET [proposer : Banks, exp : 0..MaxVer, val : Nat]
    /\ writerLog \in [1..MaxVer -> Banks \cup {None}]

\* A bank snapshots the register (possibly a stale version, since settlement
\* messages may be reordered in flight) and proposes a new value.
Propose ==
    /\ Cardinality(reqs) < 2
    /\ regVer < MaxVer
    /\ \E p \in Banks, e \in 0..regVer, v \in {regVal + 1, regVal + 2} :
         reqs' = reqs \cup {[proposer |-> p, exp |-> e, val |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVal, regVer, writerLog>>

\* Compare-and-swap succeeds only when the snapshot matches the live version.
ApplyFresh ==
    /\ \E r \in reqs :
         /\ r.exp = regVer
         /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
         /\ regVal' = r.val
         /\ writerLog' = [writerLog EXCEPT ![regVer + 1] = r.proposer]
         /\ reqs' = reqs \ {r}

\* A stale request (snapshot behind the live version) is discarded, never applied.
DropStale ==
    /\ \E r \in reqs :
         /\ r.exp < regVer
         /\ reqs' = reqs \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVal, regVer, writerLog>>

Retire ==
    /\ \E r \in reqs :
         /\ r.exp > regVer
         /\ reqs' = reqs \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVal, regVer, writerLog>>

\* Once the batch has reached its final settled version the register idles.
Settled ==
    /\ regVer = MaxVer
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVal, regVer, reqs, writerLog>>

Next == Propose \/ ApplyFresh \/ DropStale \/ Retire \/ Settled

vars == <<regVal, regVer, reqs, writerLog>>
Init ==
    /\ regVal = 0
    /\ regVer = 0
    /\ reqs = {}
    /\ writerLog = [n \in 1..MaxVer |-> None]

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed version records an authorized (fresh) writer; a stale bank's
\* proposal is never entered into the settlement chain.
AuthorizedWriterChain ==
    \A n \in 1..regVer : writerLog[n] # None
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {alpha, beta, gamma}
    MaxVer = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedWriterChain
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch is coordinated through a single shared compare-and-swap register that holds the current settled value together with a version number. To post a settlement a bank first snapshots the register's version, then submits a compare-and-swap request carrying that expected version and a proposed new value. Because settlement messages travel over a network that may reorder them, a request can arrive carrying a snapshot that is already stale by the time it is processed. The register applies a request only when its expected version exactly matches the live version, in which case it bumps the version and records the proposing bank as the authorized writer for that version. A request whose snapshot is behind the live version is a stale participant and is discarded outright, and one arriving ahead of the live version is retired unapplied. The concern is that no stale or otherwise unauthorized bank should ever have its write folded into the settlement chain.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state each committed version of the register records a genuine authorized writer, so no stale participant's settlement is ever applied.

---- MODULE W4Od13m0p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Machines, Products, MaxEpoch
VARIABLES stock, epoch, lease, lastServe

Leases == [held : BOOLEAN, prod : Products, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]
Serves == [done : BOOLEAN, prod : Products, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]

TypeInv ==
    /\ stock \in [Products -> Nat]
    /\ epoch \in [Products -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ lease \in [Machines -> Leases]
    /\ lastServe \in [Machines -> Serves]

\* A machine takes an optimistic lease, snapshotting a product's current epoch.
AcquireLease ==
    /\ \E m \in Machines, p \in Products :
         /\ ~lease[m].held
         /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![m] = [held |-> TRUE, prod |-> p, ep |-> epoch[p]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, epoch, lastServe>>

\* Commit the dispense only if the leased epoch still matches the live epoch.
Serve ==
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ lease[m].held
         /\ lease[m].ep = epoch[lease[m].prod]
         /\ stock[lease[m].prod] > 0
         /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![lease[m].prod] = stock[lease[m].prod] - 1]
         /\ lastServe' = [lastServe EXCEPT
                            ![m] = [done |-> TRUE, prod |-> lease[m].prod, ep |-> lease[m].ep]]
         /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![m].held = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch>>

\* The optimistic check failed (an intervening restock bumped the epoch); retry.
Retry ==
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ lease[m].held
         /\ lease[m].ep # epoch[lease[m].prod]
         /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![m].held = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, epoch, lastServe>>

\* Restocking bumps the product epoch, invalidating outstanding stale leases.
Restock ==
    /\ \E p \in Products :
         /\ epoch[p] < MaxEpoch
         /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch[p] + 1]
         /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![p] = stock[p] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, lastServe>>

\* A machine gives up a lease on a product that is currently out of stock.
Abandon ==
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ lease[m].held
         /\ stock[lease[m].prod] = 0
         /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![m].held = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, epoch, lastServe>>

Next == AcquireLease \/ Serve \/ Retry \/ Restock \/ Abandon

vars == <<stock, epoch, lease, lastServe>>
SomeProd == CHOOSE p \in Products : TRUE
Init ==
    /\ stock = [p \in Products |-> 1]
    /\ epoch = [p \in Products |-> 0]
    /\ lease = [m \in Machines |-> [held |-> FALSE, prod |-> SomeProd, ep |-> 0]]
    /\ lastServe = [m \in Machines |-> [done |-> FALSE, prod |-> SomeProd, ep |-> 0]]

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every recorded dispense committed at an epoch no later than its product's
\* live epoch: a stale lease can never win the commit race.
NoStaleCommit ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        lastServe[m].done =>
            lastServe[m].ep <= epoch[lastServe[m].prod]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2}
    Products = {cola, water}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleCommit
nl:
A networked fleet of vending machines shares per-product inventory guarded by optimistic locking with retry. To dispense, a machine first takes a lightweight lease that snapshots the target product's current epoch counter, then attempts to commit the sale. The commit succeeds only if the leased epoch still matches the product's live epoch; if a restock has bumped the epoch in the meantime, the optimistic check fails and the machine drops its lease and retries. A machine may also abandon a lease when the product it leased is currently out of stock. Restocking a product both increments its stock and advances its epoch, which deliberately invalidates any lease taken before the restock. Because restock and lease messages interleave and may be reordered, a machine can easily find itself holding a stale lease. The concern is that a machine holding a stale lease must never win the commit race and record a dispense as if it were current.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state each machine's last recorded dispense was committed at an epoch no later than its product's live epoch, so no stale lease ever commits.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m2p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Coordinators, Printers
VARIABLES poolOwner, vote, decision, printed, phase

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ poolOwner \in Coordinators \cup {None}
    /\ vote \in [Printers -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ decision \in {"none", "commit", "abort"}
    /\ printed \in SUBSET Printers
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting", "decided"}

\* One of two independent spooler instances grabs the shared printer pool.
AcquirePool ==
    /\ poolOwner = None
    /\ \E c \in Coordinators :
         /\ poolOwner' = c
         /\ vote' = [p \in Printers |-> "none"]
         /\ decision' = "none"
         /\ printed' = {}
         /\ phase' = "voting"

\* Phase one: each printer votes to accept or refuse the batch.
CastVote ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E p \in Printers :
         /\ vote[p] = "none"
         /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![p] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, decision, printed, phase>>

\* Coordinator decides once all printers have voted: commit iff unanimous yes.
Decide ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A p \in Printers : vote[p] # "none"
    /\ decision' = IF \A p \in Printers : vote[p] = "yes" THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"
    /\ phase' = "decided"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, vote, printed>>

\* Phase two: a printer performs the irreversible print only on a committed batch
\* and only if it itself voted yes.
Print ==
    /\ phase = "decided"
    /\ decision = "commit"
    /\ \E p \in Printers :
         /\ vote[p] = "yes"
         /\ p \notin printed
         /\ printed' = printed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, vote, decision, phase>>

\* Release the pool so the other instance can take a turn.
ReleasePool ==
    /\ phase = "decided"
    /\ poolOwner' = None
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, decision, printed>>

Next == AcquirePool \/ CastVote \/ Decide \/ Print \/ ReleasePool

vars == <<poolOwner, vote, decision, printed, phase>>
Init ==
    /\ poolOwner = None
    /\ vote = [p \in Printers |-> "none"]
    /\ decision = "none"
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ phase = "idle"

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A printer physically prints only after a committed two-phase decision and
\* only if it authorized the batch with a yes vote.
PrintOnlyOnAuthorizedCommit ==
    \A p \in printed : decision = "commit" /\ vote[p] = "yes"
====
nl:
A print shop job spooler commits each batch across its printers using a two-phase commit protocol. Two independent spooler instances share one physical printer pool, so before running a batch an instance must first grab the shared pool lock; only the current pool owner drives the protocol. In phase one every printer votes to accept or refuse the batch. Once all printers have voted, the coordinator decides: it commits only if the vote was unanimously yes, otherwise it aborts. In phase two a printer performs the irreversible physical print, but only when the decision is commit and only if that printer itself voted yes to authorize the job. When the batch finishes the instance releases the pool so the other instance may take a turn. The concern is that a printer must never physically print a batch that was not committed, nor one it did not itself authorize.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state any printer that has printed did so under a committed decision and had voted yes to authorize that batch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m9p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Zones, Controllers, TotalParts, MaxEpoch
VARIABLES onHand, transit, epoch, poolOwner

None == "none"

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET z == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN onHand[z] + SumOver(S \ {z})

TypeInv ==
    /\ onHand \in [Zones -> Nat]
    /\ transit \in Nat
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ poolOwner \in Controllers \cup {None}

\* A robot lifts one part from a zone into the transit buffer.
Pickup ==
    /\ \E z \in Zones :
         /\ onHand[z] > 0
         /\ onHand' = [onHand EXCEPT ![z] = onHand[z] - 1]
         /\ transit' = transit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, poolOwner>>

\* A robot sets a part down in some zone.
Dropoff ==
    /\ transit > 0
    /\ \E z \in Zones :
         /\ onHand' = [onHand EXCEPT ![z] = onHand[z] + 1]
         /\ transit' = transit - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, poolOwner>>

\* One of two controller instances seizes the shared reconfiguration pool.
AcquirePool ==
    /\ poolOwner = None
    /\ \E c \in Controllers : poolOwner' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onHand, transit, epoch>>

\* The owning controller reconfigures under a new epoch, shifting one part
\* between two zones (a redistribution that conserves the total).
Reconfigure ==
    /\ poolOwner # None
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E z1 \in Zones, z2 \in Zones :
         /\ z1 # z2
         /\ onHand[z1] > 0
         /\ onHand' = [onHand EXCEPT ![z1] = onHand[z1] - 1, ![z2] = onHand[z2] + 1]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<transit, poolOwner>>

ReleasePool ==
    /\ poolOwner # None
    /\ poolOwner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onHand, transit, epoch>>

Next == Pickup \/ Dropoff \/ AcquirePool \/ Reconfigure \/ ReleasePool

vars == <<onHand, transit, epoch, poolOwner>>
Init ==
    /\ onHand = [z \in Zones |-> IF z = (CHOOSE e \in Zones : TRUE) THEN TotalParts ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = 0
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ poolOwner = None

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No part is ever created or destroyed: on-hand stock across all zones plus the
\* parts currently in transit always equals the fixed fleet total.
PartsConserved ==
    SumOver(Zones) + transit = TotalParts
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Zones = {za, zb, zc}
    Controllers = {ctl1, ctl2}
    TotalParts = 2
    MaxEpoch = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PartsConserved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shuttles parts between storage zones under a controller that periodically reconfigures the layout. Robots pick a part up from a zone into a shared transit buffer and later set it down in some zone. Reconfiguration is epoch-numbered: each reconfiguration bumps a global epoch counter and redistributes one part from one zone to another, changing the layout without changing the total count. Two independent controller instances share a single reconfiguration pool, so a controller must seize the pool before it may reconfigure, and release it afterward. Parts are never manufactured or scrapped on the floor -- every part that leaves a zone is either in transit or has landed in another zone. The concern is a strict conservation law: nothing should ever be created or destroyed by any pickup, dropoff, or reconfiguration.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the sum of on-hand parts across all zones plus the parts in transit equals the fixed fleet total.

---- MODULE W4Od13m5p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Machines, Quorum, TotalCredit
VARIABLES vault, balance, votes, admin

RECURSIVE SumBal(_)
SumBal(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET m == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN balance[m] + SumBal(S \ {m})

TypeInv ==
    /\ vault \in Nat
    /\ balance \in [Machines -> Nat]
    /\ votes \in 0..Cardinality(Machines)
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN

\* A machine casts a vote toward the next credit transfer from the vault.
Vote ==
    /\ votes < Cardinality(Machines)
    /\ votes' = votes + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, balance, admin>>

\* With a quorum reached, move one credit from the vault to a machine.
CommitTransfer ==
    /\ votes >= Quorum
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ vault' = vault - 1
         /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![m] = balance[m] + 1]
    /\ votes' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED admin

\* The admin override moves a credit without waiting for a quorum.
AdminTransfer ==
    /\ admin
    /\ vault > 0
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ vault' = vault - 1
         /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![m] = balance[m] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, admin>>

\* A machine returns an unused credit to the vault.
ReturnCredit ==
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ balance[m] > 0
         /\ balance' = [balance EXCEPT ![m] = balance[m] - 1]
         /\ vault' = vault + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, admin>>

ToggleAdmin ==
    /\ admin' = ~admin
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, balance, votes>>

Next == Vote \/ CommitTransfer \/ AdminTransfer \/ ReturnCredit \/ ToggleAdmin

vars == <<vault, balance, votes, admin>>
SomeMachine == CHOOSE m \in Machines : TRUE
Init ==
    /\ vault = TotalCredit
    /\ balance = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ votes = 0
    /\ admin = FALSE

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Credit is conserved: the vault plus the sum of all machine balances always
\* equals the fixed total, whether a transfer went through quorum or the admin.
CreditConserved ==
    vault + SumBal(Machines) = TotalCredit
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {vm1, vm2, vm3}
    Quorum = 2
    TotalCredit = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CreditConserved
nl:
A vending machine network manages a shared pool of service credits held in a central vault. To move a credit out to a machine, the machines must first reach a quorum: each machine casts a vote toward the next transfer, and once a quorum of votes has accumulated the system commits one credit from the vault to some machine and resets the vote tally. A privileged admin override also exists: while engaged, an administrator may push a credit from the vault to a machine directly, bypassing the quorum. Machines may return unused credits to the vault. No matter which path a transfer takes -- quorum-approved or admin-forced -- credits are only ever moved, never minted or burned. The concern is a conservation law over the whole network: the total number of credits in existence must stay fixed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the vault balance plus the sum of all machine balances equals the fixed total credit supply.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m7p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Players, MaxVer
VARIABLES regVer, regVal, writer, valLog, crashed

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ regVer \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ regVal \in Nat
    /\ writer \in [1..MaxVer -> Players \cup {None}]
    /\ valLog \in [1..MaxVer -> Nat]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Players

\* A live player performs a compare-and-swap: it may only commit a new value if
\* its expected version equals the live version, which rules out lost updates.
CompareAndSwap ==
    /\ regVer < MaxVer
    /\ \E p \in Players, v \in {regVal + 1, regVal + 2} :
         /\ p \notin crashed
         /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
         /\ regVal' = v
         /\ writer' = [writer EXCEPT ![regVer + 1] = p]
         /\ valLog' = [valLog EXCEPT ![regVer + 1] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* A stale attempt (expected version behind the live version) is rejected without
\* touching the record, so it cannot silently clobber a newer write.
RejectStale ==
    /\ \E p \in Players : p \notin crashed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, regVal, writer, valLog, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \E p \in Players : crashed' = {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, regVal, writer, valLog>>

Settle ==
    /\ regVer = MaxVer
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regVer, regVal, writer, valLog, crashed>>

Next == CompareAndSwap \/ RejectStale \/ Crash \/ Settle

vars == <<regVer, regVal, writer, valLog, crashed>>
Init ==
    /\ regVer = 0
    /\ regVal = 0
    /\ writer = [n \in 1..MaxVer |-> None]
    /\ valLog = [n \in 1..MaxVer |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No update is lost: the live value is exactly the value of the highest committed
\* version, and every version up to the live one records a real committing writer.
NoLostUpdate ==
    /\ (regVer > 0 => regVal = valLog[regVer])
    /\ \A n \in 1..regVer : writer[n] # None
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {alice, bob, carol}
    MaxVer = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps a single shared record -- the lobby's live configuration value -- behind a compare-and-swap register with a version counter. When a player wants to update the record it performs a compare-and-swap: the write commits only if the version the player expected still equals the live version, in which case the version is bumped, the new value is stored, and the committing player is logged for that version. A stale attempt, whose expected version has fallen behind the live version, is rejected outright and leaves the record untouched, so it can never silently overwrite a newer player's update. One player may crash silently and thereafter stops issuing writes. The concern is that concurrent edits must never lose an update: the record the lobby shows must always be the newest committed write, with every intervening version properly accounted to a real writer.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the live value equals the value of the highest committed version and every version up to it records a genuine committing writer, so no update is ever lost.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Txns, MaxCap
VARIABLES phase, votes, decision, posted, capacity

Yes == "yes"

TypeInv ==
    /\ phase \in [Txns -> {"idle", "voting", "decided", "final"}]
    /\ votes \in [Txns -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ decision \in [Txns -> {"none", "commit", "abort"}]
    /\ posted \in SUBSET Txns
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

InFlight == {t \in Txns : phase[t] = "voting"}

\* Begin two-phase commit for a txn, but only while under the live slot capacity.
Begin ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "idle"
         /\ Cardinality(InFlight) < capacity
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, decision, posted, capacity>>

\* Phase-one vote: participant either approves or refuses.
CastVote ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "voting"
         /\ \E v \in BOOLEAN : votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, decision, posted, capacity>>

\* Decide commit iff the vote approved, else abort.
Decide ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "voting"
         /\ decision' = [decision EXCEPT ![t] = IF votes[t] THEN "commit" ELSE "abort"]
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "decided"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, posted, capacity>>

\* The irreversible posting of funds -- fires at most once per txn, only on commit.
Post ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "decided"
         /\ decision[t] = "commit"
         /\ t \notin posted
         /\ posted' = posted \cup {t}
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "final"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, decision, capacity>>

Abandon ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "decided"
         /\ decision[t] = "abort"
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "final"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, decision, posted, capacity>>

\* Capacity is reconfigured at runtime, never below what is already in flight.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
         /\ c >= Cardinality(InFlight)
         /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, decision, posted>>

Next == Begin \/ CastVote \/ Decide \/ Post \/ Abandon \/ Reconfigure

vars == <<phase, votes, decision, posted, capacity>>
Init ==
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ votes = [t \in Txns |-> FALSE]
    /\ decision = [t \in Txns |-> "none"]
    /\ posted = {}
    /\ capacity = 1

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The irreversible post is final and legitimate: any posted txn was committed and
\* has reached its terminal state, so funds are never posted for an uncommitted txn.
FinalityConsistent ==
    \A t \in posted : decision[t] = "commit" /\ phase[t] = "final"
====

    Txns = {tx1, tx2, tx3}
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FinalityConsistent

A bank's interbank settlement batch commits each transaction with a two-phase commit protocol across its participants. A transaction may only begin its voting phase while the number of transactions already in flight is under the current slot capacity. In phase one the participants vote to approve or refuse; the coordinator then decides commit if the vote approved and abort otherwise. The irreversible step is posting the funds: this happens at most once per transaction and only for a committed transaction, after which the transaction is final. Aborted transactions are simply retired to the final state without any posting. The slot capacity is reconfigured at runtime as load changes, but it is never lowered below the number of transactions currently in flight. The concern is that the irreversible posting of funds must never occur for a transaction that was not committed, and must never occur more than once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state every posted transaction was committed and sits in its terminal final state, so funds are never posted for an uncommitted transaction.

---- MODULE W4Od1m3p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Controllers, Runways, Flights, MaxTerm
VARIABLES leader, term, runwayFlight, flightRunway, active

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ leader \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ runwayFlight \in [Runways -> Flights \cup {None}]
    /\ flightRunway \in [Flights -> Runways \cup {None}]
    /\ active \in SUBSET Runways

\* Controllers elect (or re-elect after failover) a leader, advancing the term.
Elect ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ \E c \in Controllers :
         /\ leader' = c
         /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayFlight, flightRunway, active>>

\* The current leader fails; allocations persist but no new ones can be made.
FailLeader ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, runwayFlight, flightRunway, active>>

\* Only the leader assigns a free active runway to an unassigned flight.
Assign ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ \E r \in Runways, f \in Flights :
         /\ r \in active
         /\ runwayFlight[r] = None
         /\ flightRunway[f] = None
         /\ runwayFlight' = [runwayFlight EXCEPT ![r] = f]
         /\ flightRunway' = [flightRunway EXCEPT ![f] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, active>>

\* A flight vacates its runway.
Release ==
    /\ \E r \in Runways :
         /\ runwayFlight[r] # None
         /\ flightRunway' = [flightRunway EXCEPT ![runwayFlight[r]] = None]
         /\ runwayFlight' = [runwayFlight EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, active>>

\* Runway capacity changes at runtime; a runway may be taken out of service only
\* while it is unoccupied, and any runway may be returned to service.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E r \in Runways :
         \/ /\ r \in active
            /\ runwayFlight[r] = None
            /\ active' = active \ {r}
         \/ /\ r \notin active
            /\ active' = active \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, runwayFlight, flightRunway>>

Idle ==
    /\ term = MaxTerm
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, runwayFlight, flightRunway, active>>

Next == Elect \/ FailLeader \/ Assign \/ Release \/ Reconfigure \/ Idle

vars == <<leader, term, runwayFlight, flightRunway, active>>
Init ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ term = 0
    /\ runwayFlight = [r \in Runways |-> None]
    /\ flightRunway = [f \in Flights |-> None]
    /\ active = Runways

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Runway and flight assignment stay mutual inverses, so no runway slot is ever
\* allocated to two flights and no flight ever occupies two runways.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    /\ \A r \in Runways : runwayFlight[r] # None => flightRunway[runwayFlight[r]] = r
    /\ \A f \in Flights : flightRunway[f] # None => runwayFlight[flightRunway[f]] = f
====

An air-traffic runway allocator is run by a set of redundant controllers that elect a single leader to hand out runway slots. On failover the current leader may fail and the controllers elect a new one in a higher term; while there is no leader, existing allocations persist but no new slots may be handed out. Only the leader assigns a free, in-service runway to a flight that is not already on a runway, recording the pairing on both sides. A flight later vacates its runway, clearing the pairing. The critical concern is that the same runway slot must never be allocated to two different flights at once, and a flight must never be shown as holding two runways.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the runway-to-flight and flight-to-runway assignments are mutual inverses, so no runway is double-allocated and no flight holds two runways.

EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS N, MaxVer, MaxCap
VARIABLES tokenPos, version, contrib, capacity, pending

Nodes == 0..(N - 1)

RECURSIVE SumContrib(_)
SumContrib(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET n == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN contrib[n] + SumContrib(S \ {n})

TypeInv ==
    /\ tokenPos \in Nodes
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ contrib \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ pending \in 0..MaxCap

\* The single token circulates around the ring, granting write access in turn.
PassToken ==
    /\ tokenPos' = (tokenPos + 1) % N
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, contrib, capacity, pending>>

\* Any node may enqueue a pending update while the bounded buffer has room.
Prepare ==
    /\ pending < capacity
    /\ pending' = pending + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, version, contrib, capacity>>

\* Only the current token holder may commit a pending update to the shared record,
\* so updates serialize and none is ever lost to a concurrent writer.
Commit ==
    /\ pending > 0
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ contrib' = [contrib EXCEPT ![tokenPos] = contrib[tokenPos] + 1]
    /\ pending' = pending - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, capacity>>

\* The buffer capacity is reconfigured at runtime, never below the pending count.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
         /\ c >= pending
         /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, version, contrib, pending>>

Next == PassToken \/ Prepare \/ Commit \/ Reconfigure

vars == <<tokenPos, version, contrib, capacity, pending>>
Init ==
    /\ tokenPos = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ contrib = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ capacity = 1
    /\ pending = 0

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No update is lost: the shared version count equals the sum of every node's
\* committed contributions, so every committed write is attributed exactly once.
NoLostUpdate ==
    version = SumContrib(Nodes)

    MaxVer = 4
    MaxCap = 3

A vending machine network coordinates writes to a shared telemetry record using a token ring: a single token circulates around the ring of controller nodes, and only the node currently holding the token may commit an update to the record. Any node may enqueue a pending update into a bounded buffer, but only while the buffer has room -- when it is full, new preparations are refused. When a node holds the token it may commit one pending update, which bumps the shared version counter and credits that node's own contribution tally. The buffer's capacity is reconfigured at runtime as demand shifts, but never shrunk below the number of updates already pending. Because the token guarantees only one writer at a time, updates serialize cleanly and none is ever clobbered by a concurrent writer. The concern is that no committed update is ever lost or left unattributed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the shared version count equals the sum of every node's committed contributions, so each committed write is attributed exactly once and none is lost.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS N, MaxSeq
VARIABLES tokenPos, shedLevel, lastSeq, inbox, seqLog

Nodes == 0..(N - 1)

TypeInv ==
    /\ tokenPos \in Nodes
    /\ shedLevel \in Nat
    /\ lastSeq \in 0..MaxSeq
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET [seq : 1..MaxSeq, level : Nat]
    /\ seqLog \in [1..MaxSeq -> BOOLEAN]

\* The write token circulates around the ring of grid controllers.
PassToken ==
    /\ tokenPos' = (tokenPos + 1) % N
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shedLevel, lastSeq, inbox, seqLog>>

\* The current token holder issues a new shed command, tagged with the next
\* sequence number; the command lands in the (reorderable) inbox.
Issue ==
    /\ lastSeq < MaxSeq
    /\ (\A m \in inbox : m.seq <= lastSeq + 1)
    /\ \E lvl \in {0, 1, 2} :
         inbox' = inbox \cup {[seq |-> lastSeq + 1, level |-> lvl]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, shedLevel, lastSeq, seqLog>>

\* Because messages may be reordered, only a command that advances the sequence
\* is applied; it updates the live shed level and records its sequence.
ApplyFresh ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.seq = lastSeq + 1
         /\ shedLevel' = m.level
         /\ lastSeq' = m.seq
         /\ seqLog' = [seqLog EXCEPT ![m.seq] = TRUE]
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos>>

\* A reordered command that is not the next in sequence is buffered no longer --
\* it is discarded, never applied out of order so no newer update is lost.
DropOutOfOrder ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.seq # lastSeq + 1
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, shedLevel, lastSeq, seqLog>>

Next == PassToken \/ Issue \/ ApplyFresh \/ DropOutOfOrder

vars == <<tokenPos, shedLevel, lastSeq, inbox, seqLog>>
Init ==
    /\ tokenPos = 0
    /\ shedLevel = 0
    /\ lastSeq = 0
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ seqLog = [n \in 1..MaxSeq |-> FALSE]

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No shed update is lost: every sequence number up to the last applied one has
\* been applied exactly in order, leaving no gap where a newer command overtook.
NoLostShedUpdate ==
    \A s \in 1..MaxSeq : (s <= lastSeq) => seqLog[s]
====

    N = 3
    MaxSeq = 4
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostShedUpdate

A power-grid load shedder coordinates its shed level through a token ring of controllers: a single write token circulates the ring, and only the current holder may issue a new shed command. Each command is stamped with the next sequence number and dropped into an inbox that may deliver messages out of order. Because commands can be reordered in flight, the applier accepts a command only when its sequence number is exactly the next expected one; applying it updates the live shed level, advances the last-applied sequence, and records that sequence as done. A command that arrives out of sequence is discarded rather than applied out of order, forcing the issuer's retry path. This discipline ensures a newer shed command can never overtake and erase an earlier one that has not yet been applied. The concern is that no shed update in the accepted sequence is ever lost or skipped.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state every sequence number up to the last applied one has been applied, leaving no gap where a newer command overtook an older un-applied one.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences
CONSTANTS Blocks, TotalTrains, MaxCap
VARIABLES occ, queue, capacity, crashed

RECURSIVE SumOcc(_)
SumOcc(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN occ[b] + SumOcc(S \ {b})

TypeInv ==
    /\ occ \in [Blocks -> Nat]
    /\ queue \in Seq(Blocks \X Blocks)
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ crashed \in BOOLEAN

\* A movement authority (from-block, to-block) is enqueued while the bounded
\* queue has room; a full queue exerts backpressure and refuses new work.
EnqueueMove ==
    /\ Len(queue) < capacity
    /\ \E f \in Blocks, t \in Blocks :
         /\ f # t
         /\ occ[f] > 0
         /\ queue' = Append(queue, <<f, t>>)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, capacity, crashed>>

\* The interlocking (if not crashed) applies the head authority, moving one train
\* from its origin block to its destination block.
ApplyMove ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET a == Head(queue) IN
         /\ occ[a[1]] > 0
         /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![a[1]] = occ[a[1]] - 1, ![a[2]] = occ[a[2]] + 1]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, crashed>>

\* A stale authority whose origin has been vacated is dropped from the head.
CancelStale ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ occ[Head(queue)[1]] = 0
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, capacity, crashed>>

\* The interlocking controller crashes silently and stops applying authorities.
Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, queue, capacity>>

\* While crashed, queued authorities are flushed unexecuted (trains untouched).
FlushOnCrash ==
    /\ crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occ, capacity, crashed>>

Next == EnqueueMove \/ ApplyMove \/ CancelStale \/ Crash \/ FlushOnCrash

vars == <<occ, queue, capacity, crashed>>
Init ==
    /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = (CHOOSE e \in Blocks : TRUE) THEN TotalTrains ELSE 0]
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ capacity = 2
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Trains are conserved: no interlocking move or cancellation ever creates or
\* destroys a train, so the total occupancy across all blocks stays fixed.
TrainsConserved ==
    SumOcc(Blocks) = TotalTrains
====

CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {b1, b2, b3}
    TotalTrains = 2
    MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT TrainsConserved

A subway signalling block system moves trains between fixed track blocks by issuing movement authorities through a bounded work queue. Each authority names an origin block and a destination block, and is enqueued only while the queue has room; once the queue is full it exerts backpressure and refuses new authorities. The interlocking controller applies the authority at the head of the queue, moving one train out of its origin block and into its destination block. If the origin block has since been vacated, that stale authority is cancelled from the head rather than applied. The interlocking controller may crash silently, after which it stops applying authorities, though authorities may still be enqueued and are flushed away unexecuted while the controller is down. Trains are physical: a movement neither manufactures nor destroys one, and cancelling an authority does nothing to the trains. The concern is a strict conservation law on rolling stock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the total train occupancy summed across all blocks equals the fixed number of trains in the system.

---- MODULE W4Od8m4p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences
CONSTANTS Students, Courses, Eligible, MaxCap, SeatCap
VARIABLES queue, enrolled, term, crashed

TypeInv ==
    /\ queue \in Seq([stu : Students, crs : Courses, t : 0..2])
    /\ enrolled \in [Courses -> SUBSET Students]
    /\ term \in 0..2
    /\ crashed \in BOOLEAN

\* An eligible student's registration request enters the bounded queue, tagged
\* with the term it was issued under; a full queue refuses new requests.
Submit ==
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxCap
    /\ \E s \in Students, c \in Courses :
         /\ s \in Eligible
         /\ queue' = Append(queue, [stu |-> s, crs |-> c, t |-> term])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, term, crashed>>

\* The registrar (if not crashed) grants the head request only if the student is
\* eligible, the request is for the current term (not stale), and a seat is free.
Grant ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET r == Head(queue) IN
         /\ r.stu \in Eligible
         /\ r.t = term
         /\ Cardinality(enrolled[r.crs]) < SeatCap
         /\ enrolled' = [enrolled EXCEPT ![r.crs] = enrolled[r.crs] \cup {r.stu}]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, crashed>>

\* A stale request (issued under an earlier term) is dropped from the head.
DropStale ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Head(queue).t # term
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, term, crashed>>

\* A new registration term opens, invalidating any still-queued stale requests.
AdvanceTerm ==
    /\ term < 2
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, enrolled, crashed>>

\* The registrar node crashes silently and stops granting.
Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, enrolled, term>>

FlushOnCrash ==
    /\ crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enrolled, term, crashed>>

Next == Submit \/ Grant \/ DropStale \/ AdvanceTerm \/ Crash \/ FlushOnCrash

vars == <<queue, enrolled, term, crashed>>

    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ enrolled = [c \in Courses |-> {}]
    /\ term = 0
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized enrollment: every student enrolled in any course is one who was
\* eligible, so no ineligible or stale request ever seats a student.
OnlyEligibleEnrolled ==
    \A c \in Courses : enrolled[c] \subseteq Eligible
====
nl:
A university course-registration system processes enrollment through a bounded work queue with backpressure. A registration request may enter the queue only if the requesting student is eligible and the queue has room; a full queue refuses new requests. Each queued request is tagged with the registration term under which it was issued. The registrar processes the head request and grants a seat only when the student is still eligible, the request's term matches the current term (so it is not stale), and the course still has a free seat. A request whose term has fallen behind the current term is dropped from the head as stale. When a new registration term opens, still-queued requests from earlier terms become stale. The registrar node may crash silently and then stops granting, though queued requests can still be flushed. The concern is that no ineligible or stale request should ever result in a student being seated in a course.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state every student enrolled in any course is an eligible student, so no unauthorized or stale request ever seats anyone.

---- MODULE W4Od2m4p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Ids, MaxCap
VARIABLES pending, applied, record, capacity

\* Each update id carries a fixed weight; id 2 is a double-weight adjustment.
Delta == [i \in Ids |-> IF i = 2 THEN 2 ELSE 1]

RECURSIVE SumDelta(_)
SumDelta(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET i == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN Delta[i] + SumDelta(S \ {i})

TypeInv ==
    /\ pending \in SUBSET Ids
    /\ applied \in SUBSET Ids
    /\ record \in Nat
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

\* A robot submits a distinct inventory-delta update into the bounded queue, but
\* only while the queue has room (backpressure) and the id is genuinely new.
Submit ==
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < capacity
    /\ \E i \in Ids :
         /\ i \notin pending
         /\ i \notin applied
         /\ pending' = pending \cup {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, record, capacity>>

\* Because delivery reorders freely, any pending update may be applied next; it
\* folds its delta into the shared record exactly once and leaves the queue.
Apply ==
    /\ \E i \in pending :
         /\ pending' = pending \ {i}
         /\ applied' = applied \cup {i}
         /\ record' = record + Delta[i]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity>>

\* A pending update may be cancelled before it is applied; it is never counted.
Cancel ==
    /\ \E i \in pending :
         pending' = pending \ {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, record, capacity>>

\* The queue capacity is reconfigured at runtime, never below the pending count.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
         /\ c >= Cardinality(pending)
         /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, applied, record>>

Next == Submit \/ Apply \/ Cancel \/ Reconfigure

vars == <<pending, applied, record, capacity>>
Init ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ record = 0
    /\ capacity = 1

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No update is lost or double-counted: the shared record is exactly the sum of
\* the deltas of the applied updates, regardless of the order they arrived in.
NoLostUpdate ==
    record = SumDelta(applied)
====

    Ids = {1, 2, 3}
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate

A warehouse robot fleet reports inventory adjustments to a shared stock record through a bounded work queue with backpressure. Each robot submits a distinct update, identified by a unique id and carrying a fixed delta, but only when the queue has room; a full queue refuses new submissions. Because the messaging layer delivers freely out of order, any pending update may be the next one applied -- when applied, its delta is folded into the shared record exactly once and the update leaves the queue. An update may instead be cancelled before it is applied, in which case it is never counted. The queue's capacity is reconfigured at runtime as load changes, but is never lowered below the number of updates already pending. The concern is that reordering must never cause an update to be lost or double-counted in the shared stock record.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the shared record equals the sum of the deltas of exactly the applied updates, regardless of the order in which they arrived.

---- MODULE W4Od11m5p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Operators, Jobs, Authorized, Quorum, MaxGen
VARIABLES votes, printed, gen, inbox

TypeInv ==
    /\ votes \in [Jobs -> SUBSET Operators]
    /\ printed \in SUBSET Jobs
    /\ gen \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET [job : Jobs, op : Operators, g : 0..MaxGen]

\* An authorized operator emits a vote message for a job, tagged with the job's
\* current generation; the message lands in a reorderable inbox.
SendVote ==
    /\ Cardinality(inbox) < 3
    /\ \E o \in Operators, j \in Jobs :
         /\ o \in Authorized
         /\ j \notin printed
         /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[job |-> j, op |-> o, g |-> gen[j]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, printed, gen>>

\* A vote whose generation still matches the job is counted (messages reorder,
\* so this may fire in any order).
AcceptVote ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.g = gen[m.job]
         /\ m.job \notin printed
         /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![m.job] = votes[m.job] \cup {m.op}]
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, gen>>

\* A stale vote (generation superseded by a reset) is discarded, never counted.
DropStaleVote ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.g # gen[m.job]
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, printed, gen>>

\* A job prints once it has a quorum of accepted authorized votes.
PrintJob ==
    /\ \E j \in Jobs :
         /\ j \notin printed
         /\ Cardinality(votes[j]) >= Quorum
         /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, gen, inbox>>

\* Resetting an un-printed job bumps its generation and clears its tally, which
\* makes every vote still in flight for the old generation stale.
Reset ==
    /\ \E j \in Jobs :
         /\ j \notin printed
         /\ gen[j] < MaxGen
         /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![j] = gen[j] + 1]
         /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![j] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, inbox>>

\* A vote left in flight for a job that has already printed is discarded.
DiscardPrinted ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.job \in printed
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, printed, gen>>

\* When every job has printed and no votes remain in flight, the spooler idles.
Idle ==
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : j \in printed
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, printed, gen, inbox>>

Next == SendVote \/ AcceptVote \/ DropStaleVote \/ PrintJob \/ Reset
        \/ DiscardPrinted \/ Idle

vars == <<votes, printed, gen, inbox>>
Init ==
    /\ votes = [j \in Jobs |-> {}]
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ gen = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ inbox = {}

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized or stale approval prints a job: every printed job's tally is a
\* set of authorized operators that reached the quorum.
PrintedWereAuthorized ==
    \A j \in printed :
        /\ votes[j] \subseteq Authorized
        /\ Cardinality(votes[j]) >= Quorum
====
nl:
A print shop job spooler releases each batch only after a quorum of operators approves it. Approvals travel as vote messages over a channel that may reorder them, and each vote is tagged with the generation of the job it approves. An authorized operator sends a vote for a job that has not yet printed; when the vote is processed, it is counted only if its generation still matches the job's current generation. A vote whose generation has been superseded is stale and is discarded rather than counted. A job prints once its tally of accepted votes reaches the quorum. Resetting an un-printed job bumps its generation and clears its tally, which retroactively makes every vote still in flight for the old generation stale. The concern is that no job should ever print on the strength of unauthorized voters or stale, superseded approvals.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state every printed job's approval tally consists only of authorized operators and meets the quorum, so no stale or unauthorized vote ever releases a job.

---- MODULE W4Od11m4p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences
CONSTANTS Docs, Printers, MaxCap
VARIABLES queue, capacity, active, crashed

TypeInv ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Docs)
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap
    /\ active \in 0..Printers
    /\ crashed \in BOOLEAN

\* A document is spooled into the bounded queue only while it has room; a full
\* queue exerts backpressure and refuses the submission.
Enqueue ==
    /\ Len(queue) < capacity
    /\ \E d \in Docs : queue' = Append(queue, d)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, active, crashed>>

\* A printer (if the spooler is up) pulls the head job and begins printing it,
\* but only while a printer is free.
StartPrint ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ active < Printers
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ active' = active + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, crashed>>

\* A printer finishes a job and becomes free again.
FinishPrint ==
    /\ active > 0
    /\ active' = active - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, capacity, crashed>>

\* Capacity is reconfigured at runtime but never below the current queue length.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
         /\ c >= Len(queue)
         /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, active, crashed>>

\* The spooler crashes silently and stops starting new prints.
Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, capacity, active>>

\* While crashed, spooled jobs are flushed to relieve the full queue.
FlushOnCrash ==
    /\ crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, active, crashed>>

Next == Enqueue \/ StartPrint \/ FinishPrint \/ Reconfigure \/ Crash \/ FlushOnCrash

vars == <<queue, capacity, active, crashed>>
Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ capacity = 2
    /\ active = 0
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity is never exceeded: the spool queue never holds more than its
\* current capacity, and no more printers are ever busy than physically exist.
CapacityRespected ==
    /\ Len(queue) <= capacity
    /\ active <= Printers
====

CONSTANTS
    Docs = {da, db}
    Printers = 2
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A print shop job spooler buffers incoming documents in a bounded work queue with backpressure and hands them to a fixed set of physical printers. A document is spooled only while the queue has room; when the queue is full the spooler refuses the submission. A free printer, as long as the spooler is up, pulls the head document off the queue and begins printing it, and later finishes, freeing itself again. The queue capacity is reconfigured at runtime as demand shifts, but is never lowered below the number of documents already queued. The spooler may crash silently and then stops starting new prints, though queued jobs may still be flushed to relieve pressure. The concern is a hard resource bound: the queue must never hold more documents than its current capacity, and no more printers may ever be busy than the shop physically owns.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the queue length never exceeds the current capacity and the number of busy printers never exceeds the number of physical printers.

---- MODULE W4Od1m9p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Flights, Runways, MaxEpoch
VARIABLES phase, runwayOf, landed, epoch

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ phase \in [Flights -> {"holding", "cleared", "landed"}]
    /\ runwayOf \in [Flights -> Runways \cup {None}]
    /\ landed \in SUBSET Flights
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch

\* A holding flight is cleared onto a free runway by the controller. The
\* controller may be slow to act, but it never fails outright.
Clear ==
    /\ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways :
         /\ phase[f] = "holding"
         /\ \A g \in Flights : runwayOf[g] # r
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "cleared"]
         /\ runwayOf' = [runwayOf EXCEPT ![f] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<landed, epoch>>

\* Touchdown is the irreversible action: it fires at most once per flight, only
\* for a flight already cleared onto a runway, and latches it as landed.
Touchdown ==
    /\ \E f \in Flights :
         /\ phase[f] = "cleared"
         /\ f \notin landed
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![f] = "landed"]
         /\ landed' = landed \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayOf, epoch>>

\* An epoch-numbered reconfiguration renumbers the airspace and sends any flight
\* not yet cleared back to holding; it never disturbs a landed flight.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ phase' = [f \in Flights |-> IF phase[f] = "cleared" THEN "holding" ELSE phase[f]]
    /\ runwayOf' = [f \in Flights |-> IF phase[f] = "cleared" THEN None ELSE runwayOf[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<landed>>

\* A holding flight may be delayed further (the controller is slow, not failed).
Hold ==
    /\ \E f \in Flights : phase[f] = "holding"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, runwayOf, landed, epoch>>

Next == Clear \/ Touchdown \/ Reconfigure \/ Hold

vars == <<phase, runwayOf, landed, epoch>>
Init ==
    /\ phase = [f \in Flights |-> "holding"]
    /\ runwayOf = [f \in Flights |-> None]
    /\ landed = {}
    /\ epoch = 0

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The irreversible touchdown is consistent and final: any landed flight is in the
\* landed phase and still holds the runway it touched down on, so the landing is
\* recorded exactly once and never undone by a reconfiguration.
LandingIsFinal ==
    \A f \in landed :
        /\ phase[f] = "landed"
        /\ runwayOf[f] # None
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Flights = {f1, f2, f3}
    Runways = {r1, r2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LandingIsFinal
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator brings flights down through a small state machine. A holding flight is cleared by the controller onto a runway that no other flight currently holds; the controller may be slow to issue the clearance, but it never fails outright. Touchdown is the irreversible step: for a flight that has been cleared onto a runway, touchdown fires at most once and permanently latches the flight as landed. The airspace is periodically reconfigured under an epoch counter; a reconfiguration renumbers things and sends any flight that was merely cleared (but not yet down) back to holding, while never disturbing a flight that has already landed. The concern is that a landing, once it has irreversibly happened, must be recorded exactly once and must never be undone or duplicated by a later reconfiguration.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state every landed flight is in the landed phase and still holds the runway it touched down on, so each landing is final and recorded exactly once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m3p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Controllers, Tasks, MaxTerm
VARIABLES leader, term, leaderAt, inbox, executed

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ leader \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leaderAt \in [1..MaxTerm -> Controllers \cup {None}]
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET [task : Tasks, ldr : Controllers, trm : 1..MaxTerm]
    /\ executed \in SUBSET [task : Tasks, ldr : Controllers, trm : 1..MaxTerm]

\* Controllers elect (or on failover re-elect) a leader in a fresh, higher term.
Elect ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ \E c \in Controllers :
         /\ leader' = c
         /\ term' = term + 1
         /\ leaderAt' = [leaderAt EXCEPT ![term + 1] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, executed>>

\* The failover event: the current leader steps down, leaving no leader until the
\* next election.
StepDown ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ leader' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderAt, inbox, executed>>

\* The current leader dispatches a crane task command, tagged with its identity
\* and term; the command lands in a reorderable inbox.
Dispatch ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ \E t \in Tasks :
         inbox' = inbox \cup {[task |-> t, ldr |-> leader, trm |-> term]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderAt, executed>>

\* A command executes only if its term is the live term and it came from the
\* current leader; reordering means old commands may still be sitting in the inbox.
Execute ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.trm = term
         /\ leader = m.ldr
         /\ executed' = executed \cup {m}
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderAt>>

\* A stale command (from a superseded term) is rejected, never executed.
DropStale ==
    /\ \E m \in inbox :
         /\ m.trm # term
         /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderAt, executed>>

\* Once the final term is reached and the channel is drained, the yard idles.
Idle ==
    /\ term = MaxTerm
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderAt, inbox, executed>>

Next == Elect \/ StepDown \/ Dispatch \/ Execute \/ DropStale \/ Idle

vars == <<leader, term, leaderAt, inbox, executed>>
Init ==
    /\ leader = None
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leaderAt = [n \in 1..MaxTerm |-> None]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ executed = {}

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized or stale command runs a crane: every executed command was
\* issued in a term no later than the current one by that term's genuine leader.
NoStaleExecution ==
    \A m \in executed :
        /\ m.trm <= term
        /\ leaderAt[m.trm] = m.ldr
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {ca, cb}
    Tasks = {tk1, tk2}
    MaxTerm = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleExecution
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is coordinated by a set of controllers that elect a single leader to dispatch crane tasks. On failover the current leader may step down, and the controllers elect a new one in a fresh, higher term; each election records which controller led that term. The current leader dispatches task commands, each stamped with the leader's identity and its term, into a command channel that may reorder messages. A command executes only when its term equals the live term and it came from the current leader; because messages can be reordered, commands from superseded terms may still be sitting in the channel and must be rejected as stale rather than executed. The concern is that no crane should ever act on an unauthorized or stale command -- one from an ousted leader or an expired term.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state every executed command was issued in a term no later than the current one by that term's genuine recorded leader, so no stale or unauthorized command ever moves a crane.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m1p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
CONSTANTS N, BloodTypes, MaxUnits
VARIABLES tokenPos, stock, reserved, issued

None == -1

Nodes == 0..(N - 1)

TypeInv ==
    /\ tokenPos \in Nodes
    /\ stock \in [BloodTypes -> 0..MaxUnits]
    /\ reserved \in [BloodTypes -> Nodes \cup {None}]
    /\ issued \in [BloodTypes -> Nat]

\* The single write token circulates the ring. It may pass only when the current
\* holder has no outstanding reservation of its own to settle.
PassToken ==
    /\ \A bt \in BloodTypes : reserved[bt] # tokenPos
    /\ tokenPos' = (tokenPos + 1) % N
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, reserved, issued>>

\* Only the token holder may place a reservation on an in-stock blood type.
Reserve ==
    /\ \E bt \in BloodTypes :
         /\ reserved[bt] = None
         /\ stock[bt] > 0
         /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![bt] = tokenPos]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, stock, issued>>

\* The holder commits its own reservation, drawing one unit from stock.
Commit ==
    /\ \E bt \in BloodTypes :
         /\ reserved[bt] = tokenPos
         /\ stock[bt] > 0
         /\ issued[bt] < MaxUnits
         /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![bt] = stock[bt] - 1]
         /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![bt] = None]
         /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![bt] = issued[bt] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos>>

\* The holder may deposit a returned unit back into stock.
Deposit ==
    /\ \E bt \in BloodTypes :
         /\ stock[bt] < MaxUnits
         /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![bt] = stock[bt] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, reserved, issued>>

\* The holder may be slow, holding the token without acting; it never fails.
Dwell ==
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, stock, reserved, issued>>

Next == PassToken \/ Reserve \/ Commit \/ Deposit \/ Dwell

vars == <<tokenPos, stock, reserved, issued>>
Init ==
    /\ tokenPos = 0
    /\ stock = [bt \in BloodTypes |-> MaxUnits]
    /\ reserved = [bt \in BloodTypes |-> None]
    /\ issued = [bt \in BloodTypes |-> 0]

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No unauthorized draw: any active reservation is held by whoever currently has
\* the token, so only the token holder can ever be mid-transaction on a unit.
OnlyHolderReserves ==
    \A bt \in BloodTypes : reserved[bt] # None => reserved[bt] = tokenPos
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    BloodTypes = {oNeg, aPos}
    MaxUnits = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OnlyHolderReserves
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker serializes all changes through a token ring: a single write token circulates a ring of ward nodes, and only the node currently holding the token may touch inventory. To draw a unit, the holder first places a reservation on an in-stock blood type, then commits it, which draws one unit from stock and clears the reservation. The holder may also deposit a returned unit back into stock, and every committed draw is tallied per blood type. Crucially, the token may only be passed on when the current holder has settled all of its own reservations, so no reservation is ever left dangling for a node that no longer holds the token. A holder may be slow -- dwelling on the token without acting -- but it never fails, so the token is never lost. The concern is that no node other than the current token holder may ever be mid-transaction on a unit of blood.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state any active reservation belongs to the node that currently holds the token, so no unauthorized node is ever mid-draw.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m2p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Txns, MaxCap
VARIABLES phase, approve, record, committed, capacity

Delta == [t \in Txns |-> IF t = 2 THEN 2 ELSE 1]

TypeInv ==
    /\ phase \in [Txns -> {"idle", "voting", "done"}]
    /\ approve \in [Txns -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ record \in Nat
    /\ committed \in SUBSET Txns
    /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

RECURSIVE SumDelta(_)
SumDelta(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET t == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN Delta[t] + SumDelta(S \ {t})

InFlight == {t \in Txns : phase[t] = "voting"}

\* Begin a two-phase update to the shared page-count record, but only while under
\* the current concurrency capacity.
Begin ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "idle"
         /\ Cardinality(InFlight) < capacity
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approve, record, committed, capacity>>

\* Phase-one vote by the participants.
Vote ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "voting"
         /\ \E v \in BOOLEAN : approve' = [approve EXCEPT ![t] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, record, committed, capacity>>

\* Phase-two commit: an approved txn folds its delta into the record exactly once.
Commit ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "voting"
         /\ approve[t]
         /\ t \notin committed
         /\ record' = record + Delta[t]
         /\ committed' = committed \cup {t}
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approve, capacity>>

\* A refused txn aborts without touching the record.
Abort ==
    /\ \E t \in Txns :
         /\ phase[t] = "voting"
         /\ ~approve[t]
         /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approve, record, committed, capacity>>

\* Concurrency capacity is reconfigured at runtime, never below what is in flight.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ \E c \in 1..MaxCap :
         /\ c >= Cardinality(InFlight)
         /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, approve, record, committed>>

Next == Begin \/ Vote \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Reconfigure

vars == <<phase, approve, record, committed, capacity>>
Init ==
    /\ phase = [t \in Txns |-> "idle"]
    /\ approve = [t \in Txns |-> FALSE]
    /\ record = 0
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ capacity = 1

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No update is lost or double-applied: the shared record is always exactly the
\* sum of the deltas of the transactions that committed.
NoLostUpdate ==
    record = SumDelta(committed)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Txns = {1, 2, 3}
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A print shop job spooler maintains a shared page-count record that is updated through a two-phase commit protocol across its participants. A transaction may begin its voting phase only while the number of transactions currently in flight is under the live concurrency capacity. In phase one the participants vote to approve or refuse the update. In phase two an approved transaction commits, folding its fixed page delta into the shared record exactly once, while a refused transaction aborts and leaves the record untouched. The concurrency capacity is reconfigured at runtime as load shifts, but is never lowered below the number of transactions already in flight. The concern is that concurrent two-phase updates must never lose or double-apply a delta: the shared record must always reflect precisely the transactions that committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state the shared record equals the sum of the deltas of exactly the committed transactions, so no update is lost or double-applied.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m9p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Rooms, Procedures, MaxEpoch
VARIABLES occupant, state, roomOf, epoch, admin

None == "none"

TypeInv ==
    /\ occupant \in [Rooms -> Procedures \cup {None}]
    /\ state \in [Procedures -> {"idle", "waiting", "operating"}]
    /\ roomOf \in [Procedures -> Rooms \cup {None}]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ admin \in BOOLEAN

\* A procedure requests an operating room.
Request ==
    /\ \E p \in Procedures :
         /\ state[p] = "idle"
         /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, roomOf, epoch, admin>>

\* A waiting procedure seizes a free room and starts operating.
Acquire ==
    /\ \E p \in Procedures, r \in Rooms :
         /\ state[p] = "waiting"
         /\ occupant[r] = None
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![r] = p]
         /\ roomOf' = [roomOf EXCEPT ![p] = r]
         /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "operating"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, admin>>

\* An operating procedure finishes and vacates its room.
Finish ==
    /\ \E p \in Procedures :
         /\ state[p] = "operating"
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![roomOf[p]] = None]
         /\ roomOf' = [roomOf EXCEPT ![p] = None]
         /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, admin>>

\* The admin override forcibly clears an operating procedure out of its room
\* (an emergency bump), returning it to waiting.
AdminPreempt ==
    /\ admin
    /\ \E p \in Procedures :
         /\ state[p] = "operating"
         /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![roomOf[p]] = None]
         /\ roomOf' = [roomOf EXCEPT ![p] = None]
         /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, admin>>

\* An epoch-numbered reconfiguration of the theatre suite sends all merely
\* waiting procedures back to idle; operating procedures are untouched.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ state' = [p \in Procedures |-> IF state[p] = "waiting" THEN "idle" ELSE state[p]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, roomOf, admin>>

ToggleAdmin ==
    /\ admin' = ~admin
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, state, roomOf, epoch>>

Next == Request \/ Acquire \/ Finish \/ AdminPreempt \/ Reconfigure \/ ToggleAdmin

vars == <<occupant, state, roomOf, epoch, admin>>
Init ==
    /\ occupant = [r \in Rooms |-> None]
    /\ state = [p \in Procedures |-> "idle"]
    /\ roomOf = [p \in Procedures |-> None]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ admin = FALSE

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion of the critical resource: any operating procedure holds a room
\* that records it as the sole occupant, so two procedures can never operate in the
\* same room at once.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A p \in Procedures :
        state[p] = "operating" =>
            /\ roomOf[p] # None
            /\ occupant[roomOf[p]] = p
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Rooms = {or1, or2}
    Procedures = {p1, p2, p3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler assigns procedures to a small set of theatres. A procedure first requests a room, moving from idle to waiting; a waiting procedure then seizes a free room and begins operating, which records it as that room's occupant. When it finishes it vacates the room and returns to idle. A privileged admin override exists: in an emergency the administrator may forcibly preempt an operating procedure, clearing it out of its room and sending it back to waiting so the room frees up. The theatre suite is periodically reconfigured under an epoch counter, which sends all merely-waiting procedures back to idle while never disturbing a procedure already operating. The overriding safety concern is exclusive use of each theatre: two procedures must never be operating in the same room at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: in every reachable state any operating procedure holds a room that records it as the sole occupant, so no two procedures ever operate in the same room simultaneously.

---- MODULE W4Od3m7p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Accounts, Instances, Total, MaxVer
VARIABLES acct, transit, poolOwner, poolVer

None == "none"

RECURSIVE SumAcct(_)
SumAcct(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET a == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN acct[a] + SumAcct(S \ {a})

TypeInv ==
    /\ acct \in [Accounts -> Nat]
    /\ transit \in Nat
    /\ poolOwner \in Instances \cup {None}
    /\ poolVer \in 0..MaxVer

\* A settlement instance seizes the shared pool via compare-and-swap on the pool's
\* version register: it succeeds only if its expected version is the live one.
AcquirePool ==
    /\ poolOwner = None
    /\ poolVer < MaxVer
    /\ \E i \in Instances, exp \in 0..MaxVer :
         /\ exp = poolVer
         /\ poolOwner' = i
         /\ poolVer' = poolVer + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acct, transit>>

\* The pool owner debits one unit from a funded account into the transit buffer.
Debit ==
    /\ poolOwner # None
    /\ \E a \in Accounts :
         /\ acct[a] > 0
         /\ acct' = [acct EXCEPT ![a] = acct[a] - 1]
         /\ transit' = transit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, poolVer>>

\* The pool owner credits a unit from the transit buffer into some account.
Credit ==
    /\ poolOwner # None
    /\ transit > 0
    /\ \E a \in Accounts :
         /\ acct' = [acct EXCEPT ![a] = acct[a] + 1]
         /\ transit' = transit - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<poolOwner, poolVer>>

ReleasePool ==
    /\ poolOwner # None
    /\ poolOwner' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acct, transit, poolVer>>

\* When the register has reached its final version and no instance holds the pool,
\* the batch is settled and idles.
Settled ==
    /\ poolVer = MaxVer
    /\ poolOwner = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acct, transit, poolOwner, poolVer>>

Next == AcquirePool \/ Debit \/ Credit \/ ReleasePool \/ Settled

vars == <<acct, transit, poolOwner, poolVer>>
SomeAcct == CHOOSE a \in Accounts : TRUE
Init ==
    /\ acct = [a \in Accounts |-> IF a = SomeAcct THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ transit = 0
    /\ poolOwner = None
    /\ poolVer = 0

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Money is conserved: the total across all accounts plus whatever is mid-transfer
\* in the transit buffer always equals the fixed settlement total.
